title: ABC de las Sanciones Propias que impondrá la JEP
inspected: Questions on restorative component, participation and effective restrictions; web lines109–117
data_labels_language: Official Spanish institutional explanation; no ML dataset or performance experiment.
supported_claim: Restorative sanctions combine victim participation, truth and responsibility with restoration of rights and social relations.
limitation: Authority for task interpretation, not an empirical gold similarity matrix or sufficient-remedy label.
evidence_weight: strong normative authority; no novelty claim

title: Lineamientos complementarios en materia de sanciones propias y TOAR
inspected: Comunicado153, paragraphs on participation and evaluation of correspondence; web lines94–104
data_labels_language: Official Spanish communiqué about Tribunal guidance, not full adjudication or model evaluation.
supported_claim: Victims participate in sanction design, structuring and execution; correspondence assessment links facts, recognition, evidence and proposed sanctions.
limitation: A retrieval label should distinguish a proposal from judicial assessment or actual implementation.
evidence_weight: strong normative authority; precise case adequacy still expert-dependent

title: Participación en la formulación de políticas: sanción propia y TOAR
inspected: TOAR definition and quoted guidelines pp5,10–11; web lines98–117
data_labels_language: Official Spanish institutional page; participating victims and comparecientes are specified stakeholders.
supported_claim: TOAR is the restorative component; sanctions also involve liberty/right restrictions. Victim dialogue and effective participation matter.
limitation: Do not conflate any punishment with victim-specific repair or infer victim endorsement from a positive action description.
evidence_weight: strong normative authority; overlaps S01/S02, not independent empirical evidence

authors: Theo van Boven / UN Audiovisual Library of International Law
title: Introductory note: Basic Principles and Guidelines on Right to Remedy and Reparation
inspected: Structure and key provisions, principles15,19–23; web lines67–97
data_labels_language: Official interpretive note to international instrument; not a current case-specific ruling.

title: What Comes After Harm? Mapping Reparative Actions in AI through Justice Frameworks
inspected: Methods: taxonomy development, scaling, limitations; Table1; AppendixC/D identified
data_labels_language: 1060 AIAAIC incident records; purposive200-record taxonomy sample; GPT-4Turbo multilabel coding checked against human samples.
supported_claim: Stakeholder-action extraction supports four goals: acknowledgment, attribution, remedy and reform.
limitation: Public incident reporting omits private/underreported responses; LLM coding identifies patterns rather than replacing human interpretation.
evidence_weight: strong close computational prior art; AI incidents differ from Colombian hearings

title: Finding a way to live with the past: self-repair, informal repair, and reparations in transitional justice
data_labels_language: Qualitative purposive interviews with250+ individuals across seven post-conflict contexts, including42Colombia; English publication.
supported_claim: Victim agency and continuing self/informal repair challenge the assumption that formal measures fully resolve harm.
limitation: Interviews are not representative population estimates; needs and participation can change over time.
evidence_weight: strong empirical challenge to inverse/mirror assumption

title: Algorithmic reparation
inspected: A critical read on FML; final substantive discussion and conclusion; footnote3
data_labels_language: Conceptual, interdisciplinary critique and examples; not a new JEP retrieval benchmark.
supported_claim: Reparative computing and structural/historical redress are established ideas beyond debiasing.
limitation: A technically fairer representation is not itself reparative justice; contextual social institutions remain part of the target.
evidence_weight: strong conceptual prior art; no evidence of conditional harm-remedy translation

title: Reparations of the horse? Algorithmic reparation and overspecialized remedies
inspected: Part1 five reparation forms; Part2 too-specific target; web lines93–105,121–132
data_labels_language: Conceptual analysis using legal/social examples; not a model or shared benchmark.
supported_claim: Narrowing the target to the algorithm can miss underlying structural causes or offer only partial redress.
limitation: An elegant embedding relation may repair the wrong deficit; retain the scope and causal target of each candidate response.

title: Learning Analogy-Preserving Sentence Embeddings for Answer Selection
data_labels_language: English WikiQA/TrecQA subsets; supervised positive/negative relational quadruples and shared BiGRU encoder.
supported_claim: Learning analogous sentence-pair shifts and ranking responses by relation similarity already has direct precedent.
limitation: Question-answer prototypes differ from victim-specific response adequacy; best-prototype selection and candidate construction are important controls.
evidence_weight: strong counterexample to novelty of sentence relation-vector training

title: Sentence Analogies: Linguistic Regularities in Sentence Embeddings
data_labels_language: English lexical-derived and NLI-derived analogy data, including entailment, negation and passivization.
supported_claim: Sentence analogies and perturbation-based evaluation predate this project; candidate exclusion can change apparent performance.
limitation: A successful arithmetic completion may reflect candidate constraints or topical similarity, not a transferable moral relation.
